summary: The CHOICE for Veterans Act of 2025 amends title 38, United States Code, to regulate fee agreements and representation for initial and supplemental claims for benefits administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs. The bill establishes rules for accredited agents and attorneys, sets fee caps, outlines prohibited practices, provides penalties for unauthorized fees, mandates reporting requirements for the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Comptroller General, and extends certain limits on pension payments.

affected_groups.effect: Receive new notifications regarding free and accredited assistance options, online fee warnings, protection against certain fees for initial claims, and regulated fee structures for agents and attorneys.

Subject to new application requirements, conditional recognition rules, mandatory fee agreement filings, increased continuing legal education requirements, specific prohibitions on business practices, and potential audits or penalties.
Required to update websites, publish lists of accredited persons, develop standard forms, issue regulations, conduct reviews, and submit multiple reports to Congress.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to notify claimants filing initial or supplemental claims about the availability of accredited persons and free recognized organizations, and to maintain an online list of accredited persons and a reporting system for unaccredited individuals charging fees.
Establishes a temporary and conditional recognition process (up to one year and renewable) for agents and attorneys if the Secretary cannot verify qualifications within 180 days.

Regulates fee agreements for initial and supplemental claims, capping fees at the lesser of $12,500 (adjusted for inflation) or five times the monthly increase in awarded benefits, and requiring contingency terms and payment options if fees exceed past-due benefits.

Prohibits agents and attorneys from charging fees for service-connected chronic conditions or claims filed while on active duty, and bans practices such as failing to protect client data under HIPAA, selling personal data, or using overseas call centers.

Imposes criminal penalties, fines, and imprisonment for unaccredited individuals charging unauthorized fees, and applies specific fines and temporary bans for violations committed during conditional recognition.
Directs the Comptroller General to review the agent and attorney recognition process and report findings and recommendations to congressional committees within one year.
Establishes federal preemption, stating that the Act supersedes any inconsistent State laws.
missing_information: Exact amount of the assessment the Secretary may charge and collect from certain agents and attorneys.
Specific regulatory definitions for 'preparation, presentation, or prosecution' to be written by the General Counsel.

The bill establishes rules for accredited agents and attorneys, sets fee caps, outlines prohibited practices, provides penalties for unauthorized fees, mandates reporting requirements for the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Comptroller General, and extends certain limits on pension payments.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters the legal and administrative framework governing veteran benefits claims by explicitly permitting and regulating fee agreements for initial claims while setting strict consumer protections, oversight mechanisms, and penalties for representatives.
